name: coredata
title: Extracting the Core Data of Objects

origin.description: coredata drops the index, frequency, and zoo class and returns the observations. A matrix stays a matrix, filled down columns.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An object. A zoo series stores observations separately from its index.

origin.details: coredata drops the index, frequency, and zoo class and returns the observations. A matrix stays a matrix, filled down columns.
origin.value: The observations. A zoo matrix is returned with its dimensions.
origin.example:
x <- zoo(matrix(1:6, ncol = 2), 1:3)
cat(paste(as.vector(coredata(x)), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: coredata drops the index, frequency, and zoo class and returns the observations. A matrix stays a matrix, filled down columns.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An object. A zoo series stores observations separately from its index.

translation.details: coredata drops the index, frequency, and zoo class and returns the observations. A matrix stays a matrix, filled down columns.
translation.value: The observations. A zoo matrix is returned with its dimensions.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from zoo.series import Zoo
from zoo.coredata import coredata
x = Zoo(np.array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]).reshape((3, 2), order="F"), [1, 2, 3])
print(" ".join(str(int(v)) for v in np.ravel(coredata(x), order="F")))
